subject.title: fix(cli): abort reaps autonomous executor process trees

question: Which containment mechanism should make abort authoritative for turn-owned descendants that leave the executor's original process group?
rationale: Process-group isolation does not cover the linked credentialed-executor incident, while a stronger mechanism must preserve intentional background lifetimes and work consistently across supported platforms and CLI backends.

options.title: Require complete turn containment
options.body: Use an OS-backed or tracked turn owner that can terminate escaped descendants before this PR becomes merge-ready.

options.title: Limit and disclose abort semantics
options.body: Retain process-group-only cleanup but explicitly enumerate survivors and narrow the user-visible promise that abort stops execution.

recommendation.title: Require complete turn containment
recommendation.body: Use an OS-backed or tracked turn owner that can terminate escaped descendants before this PR becomes merge-ready.

likelyOwner.reason: The process-supervisor architecture and Codex-like process-lifetime model originated in this person's merged refactor, making them the strongest history-backed routing candidate for the ownership decision.
